source.title: Measuring Sparse Autoencoder Feature Sensitivity
source.authors: Claire Tian; Katherine Tian; Nathan Hu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether SAE features activate on newly generated, semantically similar inputs. Its results qualify the idea that SAE features are complete or consistently reliable units, though it does not test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study does not test whether sparse features overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, whether extra features are dropped, or whether importance determines feature allocation. It also does not measure how features are distributed across neurons or compare SAE features with ground-truth model features. Cited findings and literature claims are not rows. The study's prompt and filtering choices are not independent results.
record.test_reason: The study measures how reliably SAE features fire on new text that humans judge indistinguishable from their activating examples. Many interpretable features fail this test, and failure grows with SAE width. That bears on the completeness and reliability part of V5 (SAE features as the model's units). It does not test superposition geometry, capacity accounts or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that sensitivity is a distinct axis of SAE feature quality and that many interpretable features have poor sensitivity. They also find average sensitivity declines with SAE width across 7 variants, which they frame as a new challenge for scaling SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures SAE feature sensitivity using generated semantically similar text; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported sensitivity varies with SAE width and sparsity; the GemmaScope results are reported as robust to feature-selection cutoff, and the study reports a feature-frequency-controlled analysis with the same width trend.

fits_no_version.finding: In the GemmaScope 1M SAE, sensitivity correlates weakly with frequency (ρ=-0.06) and max decoder cosine similarity (ρ=0.06), and moderately with auto-interp score (ρ=0.24).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature sensitivity is a quality dimension distinct from interpretability, frequency and decoder overlap.

record.problems: The study evaluates only features with at least 15 activations in 2 million tokens and filters out features that activate on fewer than 90% of shortened examples; the authors note this may bias results toward simpler features. The human evaluation has 102 examples and focuses on high-auto-interpretability features. Scaling plots do not provide uncertainty estimates in the reported text.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible results omitted. Related results such as the sensitivity-by-sparsity trend and correlations with interpretability, frequency, and decoder cosine similarity were not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure the tested V5 aspect.

untested.parts: All of it: toy models, overlap and near-orthogonality, sparsity transition, geometry.
All of it: capacity competition and allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All of it: polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
Whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs recover ground-truth features. The study assumes SAE features exist and only evaluates their sensitivity.
Stability across seeds or training runs, and canonicality. Feature splitting and absorption are discussed only via citations.
All of it: one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: At fixed width, average sensitivity rises with L0, i.e. with more active features. This holds in GemmaScope and across SAEBench architectures, so feature completeness depends on the sparsity choice.
missing.locator: Section 6.1 Fig 6; Section 6.2 Fig 7; Appendix C Fig 11

missing.what: The width decline persists after reweighting features to a common frequency distribution.
The share of features that fail to fire on their own truncated activating examples rises with width, from 51.0% at 65K to 78.8% at 1M (GemmaScope).
Vanilla ReLU SAEs consistently show low sensitivity. Matryoshka SAEs also show the negative scaling with width.

record.verdict_notes: The link to V5 is indirect: the study frames sensitivity as feature quality, not as a test of canonical units. Results are restricted to frequent features (≥15 activations in 2M tokens) that survive the truncation filter, which may bias toward simpler features. The human validation covers only 102 items, all from high-interp features.

versions.untested_parts: Overlapping directions, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry in toy networks.
Polysemanticity, competition for capacity, and the allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity occurs without capacity pressure.
The study evaluates SAE feature sensitivity, not feature distribution across neurons or whether SAE dictionaries recover ground-truth features.

Sensitivity to similar generated text bears on the completeness and reliability aspect, but the study does not establish whether SAE features are stable across conditions or canonical units of the model's representation.
The study does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.measure: Number of high-auto-interpretability features with sensitivity at or below the stated cutoffs

rows.check: The row is correct: 82 of 1,347 high-interp features have sensitivity ≤0.5 and 23 have ≤0.2. Most features score well, so completeness holds only partially. The baseline is the overall distribution in Fig 3a, not a control condition.

rows.subject: Human annotators
rows.operation_detail: Rated similarity between generated texts that failed to activate a feature and that feature's activating examples

conditions.value: Generated text from the study's method that failed to activate the feature

rows.measure: Proportion rated indistinguishable from the activating examples
rows.value: 79% rated indistinguishable; only one of 62 rated unrelated
rows.note: This human assessment supports the authors' interpretation that low feature sensitivity is not simply due to generated texts being unrelated to the feature examples.
rows.check: This is the method's human validation (a control). Raters judged generated texts nearly as related as ground truth (79% vs 83% indistinguishable). It shows the failing texts are valid tests but does not itself measure feature completeness. It should not carry a V5 state.

relation.reason: The study directly measures whether SAE features activate reliably on relevant inputs, bearing on V5.

tranche.reason: Incomplete sensitivity and declining sensitivity with dictionary width qualify V5's completeness claim.

source_check.notes: Results concern frequent features surviving truncation-based filtering; human validation covers a sample of generated texts. Cross-seed stability and canonical dictionary identity are untested; the authors' conclusion paraphrase is accurate.

statements.correction: V5: limits_scope; canonical GemmaScope 1M SAE, Gemma 2 2B layer 12; 1,347 features with auto-interpretability ≥0.9; 82 with sensitivity ≤0.5; 23 with sensitivity ≤0.2; most features score well on sensitivity; incomplete activation on semantically similar generated inputs.
statements.problem: The counts and conditions for this study are correct, but the challenges label overstates its mixed results. Low sensitivity does not separately establish that feature meaning changes with input distribution.
